name: The Silent Override (with distractors)
A:

The laboratory was founded in 1998 and currently employs forty-two researchers.
Last spring, the safety officer completed a two-week certification course in chemical handling.
Procedures classified as low-risk may bypass the safety officer's review.

Can the procedure be implemented under the laboratory's rules?

name: The Delayed Signal (with distractors)
A:
A monitoring system records electrical activity in a remote facility.
The facility is located about forty kilometers from the nearest town.
The monitoring software was upgraded to a new version in March.
The facility's backup generator automatically activates whenever the primary power supply fails.
At 09:14, the monitoring system recorded a sudden increase in electrical activity.
The primary power supply failed at 09:12.
The monitoring system has a fixed reporting delay of four minutes.
Could the recorded increase have resulted from the generator activating in response to the power failure?

name: The Definition Shift (control pair) (with distractors)
A:
A company evaluates the reliability of its automated systems using an internal classification standard.
The company was founded in 2011 and has offices in three countries.
Both systems were developed by the same engineering team over eighteen months.
Under this standard, a system is considered reliable if it completes at least 95% of assigned operations without requiring human intervention.
System Alpha completed 970 out of 1,000 operations without intervention.
System Beta completed 940 out of 1,000 operations without intervention.
Systems meeting the reliability threshold are eligible for independent deployment.
The threshold includes systems that achieve exactly the specified percentage.
Which systems are eligible for independent deployment?
B:

name: The Unchanged Outcome (with distractors)

name: The Invisible Selection Bias (with distractors)
A:
A university evaluates a new educational program.
The university has offered courses in this subject for over thirty years.
The new program uses online materials and weekly group discussions.
One hundred students participated in the program.
Ninety students completed the program successfully.
The university compares this result with an earlier group in which 70% of students completed a traditional program.
Students in both groups were randomly assigned, and both groups were evaluated using identical criteria.
Can the university conclude that the new program achieved a higher observed completion rate?
B:
